problem: Cloud-based pipelines for always-on, proactive embodied AI assistants suffer from latency, bandwidth and privacy limits, and prior systems do not offer a fully on-device, plug-and-play stack.
motivation: An always-on contextual assistant on a mobile robot needs real-time, privacy-preserving perception, reasoning and action without cloud reliance. Running fully on-device makes low-latency free-form user-robot interaction feasible on robots with only basic locomotion.
key_idea: A fully on-device hierarchical embodied intelligence system combining a real-time StreamBrain, modular skill experts, and a dynamic scene-episode memory.
insight: Based only on the abstract: the hierarchical split into a real-time streaming brain, pluggable skill experts and a scene-episode memory is claimed to enable up to 7.3x faster local processing and plug-and-play deployment across tasks. No ablations are available in the abstract to verify this.
method: StreamBrain: real-time streaming perception and reasoning core running on-device
Modular skill experts: pluggable skills for tasks such as semantic navigation and multimodal interaction
Dynamic scene-episode memory: stores scene and episode information for spatial memory recall
On-device deployment: runs without external cloud infrastructure, claimed up to 7.3x faster local processing

setting.observation: not specified (multimodal streaming perception on a mobile robot)
setting.action_space: basic locomotion of a mobile robot

numbers_note: abstract only; the only quantitative claim is up to 7.3x faster local processing, with no benchmark results
results: The demo claims up to 7.3x faster local processing and shows a mobile robot with only basic locomotion doing real-time free-form user-robot interaction fully on-device. No benchmark numbers or baselines are given in the abstract.
limitations: Demo paper; no quantitative benchmark evaluation is reported in the abstract
Models, hardware and baselines for the 7.3x speedup are unspecified
